title: Linear Momentum, Impulse & Conservation of Linear Momentum
notes: Linear momentum is p = mv. It is a vector, so a sign convention is part of the answer. The usual choice is to take one direction as positive and the opposite direction as negative.

Impulse is the product of a force and the time it acts, when the force is constant. The impulse–momentum relation says F Δt = Δp = mv − mu. A large force for a short time can change the momentum as much as a small force acting longer.
If the net external force on a system is zero, the total momentum of the system stays constant. Internal forces come in third-law pairs and do not change the total momentum.
For two bodies along one line, m1 u1 + m2 u2 = m1 v1 + m2 v2. This is conservation of momentum. It is true for collisions even when kinetic energy is not conserved.
An explosion or a gun firing is the same law. Before the event the total momentum can be zero. After it, the pieces have equal and opposite momenta so the vector sum is still zero.

Kinetic energy is conserved only in an elastic collision. Momentum conservation does not need that extra condition. In a perfectly inelastic collision the bodies stick, and you still use momentum conservation, with a shared final velocity.

**Impulse relations (classified)**

| Quantity | Formula | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Impulse | J = FΔt = Δp | N·s | Force integrated over time |
| Momentum | p = mv | kg·m/s | Quantity of motion |
| Average force | F = Δp/Δt | N | Smaller Δt → larger F |
| Area under F–t | Equals impulse | — | Graph reading |

**Impulse in safety design**

| Design | Strategy | Physics |
|---|---|---|
| Airbag | Increases Δt | Same Δp, smaller F |
| Crumple zone | Extends stopping distance | Force spread over time |
| Bending knees | Longer landing time | Reduces peak force |
| Cricket follow-through | Longer contact | Gentler catch |

exercises.question: A 2.0 kg body moving at 4.0 m/s collides with and sticks to a 2.0 kg body at rest. Find the common speed.
steps: Take the initial direction of the moving body as positive.
The bodies stick, so there is one final velocity v.
Conservation gives 4.0 v = 8.0, so v = 2.0 m/s.

topicTitle: Linear Momentum, Impulse & Conservation of Linear Momentum

subtopics.name: Momentum
points: p = mv, a vector in the direction of velocity
Newton's second law in its general form is F = dp/dt

subtopics.name: Impulse
points: Impulse = F x t = change in momentum
Area under a force-time graph gives impulse
Explains why airbags and crumple zones reduce injury — longer time, smaller force

subtopics.name: Law of conservation of momentum
points: Total momentum of an isolated system stays constant
Follows from Newton's third law — internal forces cancel in pairs
Applies to all collisions and explosions

subtopics.name: Collisions
points: Elastic: momentum and kinetic energy both conserved
Inelastic: momentum conserved, kinetic energy lost to heat and deformation
Perfectly inelastic: bodies stick together and move with common velocity

subtopics.name: Coefficient of restitution
points: e = relative velocity of separation / relative velocity of approach
e = 1 for elastic, e = 0 for perfectly inelastic
Energy loss relates directly to e

subtopics.name: Centre of mass view
points: In a collision the centre of mass continues unaffected by internal forces
Working in the centre-of-mass frame simplifies collision problems
Explains why total momentum is conserved even when energy is not
